name: Digital Twins of Production
blurb: Simulating plants and processes with AI.
title: Digital Twins of Production
answer: Digital twins model a process or whole production line so changes can be tested in simulation before the plant. Roche has built digital twins of production lines with NVIDIA Omniverse as part of AI factories spanning research and manufacturing.

reading.body:
A digital twin lets a production change be tested in simulation before it is made in the plant, and Roche has built them for production lines using NVIDIA Omniverse.

The pattern is that the twin sits upstream of the physical change. A process or a whole line is modeled, changes are run against the model, and only then does the plant itself move. Roche's twins are described as part of AI factories that span research and manufacturing, so the same modeling approach is being applied across the two ends of the business rather than in one isolated plant.

For AI specifically, the constraint is data rather than simulation software. A twin is only as good as the process data behind it, which is why the practical advice is to start with one well instrumented line instead of attempting a site-wide model. That is a compute and instrumentation problem before it is a modeling problem, and it is the step that determines whether the twin reflects the plant or merely approximates it.

The data covers one named company and one named platform, with no figures on line counts, cost, or measured outcomes. It does not say how far the Roche work has scaled, whether the twins run in production or pilot, or what results they produced.

explainer:
A digital twin is a virtual model of a physical process, piece of equipment or entire facility, kept in sync with real data from sensors and systems. Engineers use it to test changes, such as new settings, layouts or schedules, in simulation before touching the real line, and to train AI controllers safely.

In pharma, twins help with process development and scale up, capacity planning, operator training, and predicting how changes affect quality. Their accuracy depends on good process understanding and reliable data, so they work best on well instrumented processes. Starting with a single line or unit operation, proving value, then extending is the usual path.
